Kulykiv Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Lviv Oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. The Council of Four Lands, the supreme Jewish self-governing body of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, held meetings in Kulykiv several times during the 17th and 18th centuries — the same body referenced at Kremenets elsewhere in this collection. At the beginning of the 19th century, Rabbi Shlomo Kluger (1785–1869) served simultaneously as head of the religious court of Brody and as rabbi of Kulykiv, Rava-Ruska, and Lublin all at once — an extraordinary span of concurrent rabbinic responsibilities across four different towns, documented at his other posts elsewhere in this collection. On November 25, 1942, 586 Jews were deported to the Bełżec death camp, and the remnants of the community were expelled to the Zhovkva ghetto.
